utility_name: Virginia Electric & Power Co (Dominion Energy Virginia)
rule_summary: Dominion's residential/small-C&I tariff sub-caps nonresidential systems at 1 MW (below the 3 MW statewide statutory ceiling). Following the SCC's April 30, 2026 final order (Case No. PUR-2025-00079), Dominion is rolling out a 'NEM 2.0' tariff for customers who interconnect after the order's effective date: 1:1 kWh crediting and 12-month (annual) netting are preserved, but the year-end net-excess-generation cash-out rate rises to $0.05829/kWh (includes a new $0.01/kWh credit for avoided RPS/REC compliance cost) and a $1/month administrative fee applies. The SCC rejected Dominion's proposed $100-750 application fee and its proposed 30-minute netting/dollar-based interval crediting. Pre-order NEM 1.0 customers remain grandfathered indefinitely and may switch to NEM 2.0 only if it becomes more favorable to them. Low-income customers may choose whichever tariff (legacy or NEM 2.0) is more favorable. Separately, the SCC-authorized standby charge threshold rises from 15 kW AC to 20 kW AC effective 7/1/2026 under HB 1255.
nem_aggregate_cap: 6% of prior-year peak load statewide; Dominion-specific current subscription level not published in sources reviewed
export_credit_value: Legacy (NEM 1.0): year-end excess at avoided cost (~3.5c/kWh, last published 2019 figure); NEM 2.0 (new interconnections after ~mid-2026): $0.05829/kWh year-end excess cash-out, effective per April 30, 2026 SCC order
ic_application_fee: $0 application fee (SCC rejected Dominion's proposed $100-750 fee); $1/month administrative fee applies to NEM 2.0 customers only
ic_study_trigger_kw: Not published as a distinct kW threshold beyond standard Level 1/2/3 SGF review tiers
external_disconnect: Required per Dominion Terms and Conditions Section XXV for net-metered generating facilities
grid_charging_allowed: Yes-but-not-credited (grid-charged battery discharge is not distinguished from PV export in metering; Off-Peak Plan customers have export credited at the on/off/super-off-peak rate of the interval generated)
standby_charge: $2.79/kW distribution + $1.40/kW transmission standby charge per month on Schedules 1/1G (approx.); $4.19/kW distribution + $1.32/kW transmission on Schedule 1S; charge is based on the customer's peak monthly kW pulled from the grid, not on generation
standby_threshold_kw: 20 kW AC effective 7/1/2026 (raised from 15 kW AC under HB 1255; was 10 kW AC 2011-earlier revision)
storage_specific_notes: Adding a battery to an existing net-metered system does not by itself void grandfathering under the April 2026 SCC order language ('nothing...shall affect any eligible customer-generator...who interconnect before the effective date'), but any change in interconnected AC nameplate capacity requires a new interconnection application per company practice, and if the resulting aggregate AC capacity crosses the 15/20 kW standby-charge threshold it will newly trigger the standby charge — this specific battery-retrofit scenario is not explicitly addressed in Dominion's public net metering materials and should be confirmed directly with the company (flagged in gaps file). AC-coupled vs DC-coupled battery treatment and metering configuration requirements are not detailed in sources reviewed.

rule_summary: SCC Final Order (Aug. 29, 2025) largely rejected APCo's proposed net metering overhaul. APCo had sought to cut net-excess-generation compensation by ~70% (from ~8c/kWh to as low as 4.7c/kWh) and to add new grid-connection/standby charges; the SCC rejected the standby charge entirely and rejected switching from 12-month to hourly netting. Full retail 1:1 credit for self-consumed solar within the 12-month banking period is preserved. Net excess generation (true excess beyond annual consumption) is now compensated at a rate that includes REC value and exceeds the prior default PJM LMP-based avoided-cost rate. The 6% aggregate cap was retained (APCo had sought a reduction).
nem_aggregate_cap: 6% of prior-year peak load (state default; APCo-specific subscription level not published in sources reviewed)
export_credit_value: Net excess generation (annual true-up) compensated at avoided-cost/PJM LMP-based rate plus REC value, now higher than the prior straight avoided-cost figure (~3.5c/kWh, 2019); full retail 1:1 credit preserved for self-consumed generation
standby_charge: None — the SCC's August 29, 2025 order explicitly rejected APCo's proposed standby/grid-connection charge; monthly Basic (customer) charge remains $7.96/month, unchanged by the order
standby_threshold_kw: Not applicable (no standby charge in APCo Virginia territory as of the 2025 order)
storage_specific_notes: Not directly addressed in sources reviewed for the battery-retrofit/grandfathering question; APCo's standard Net Metering Terms and Conditions state system sizing must not exceed annual usage to retain rollover eligibility, so a battery addition that increases interconnected AC capacity could still trigger a new interconnection review even though no standby charge exists in APCo territory.

rule_summary: Following the PSC's August 2025 base rate case order, AEP-WV ended 1:1 retail net metering for new customers. Customers whose net metering interconnection APPLICATION was submitted on or before February 28, 2026 are grandfathered onto full 1:1 retail crediting. Customers who apply after that date are subject to a fixed export credit of approximately 12.4 cents/kWh (67-75% of full retail rate, roughly a 27% cut from the effective 1:1 value) instead of 1:1 crediting. The PSC granted APCo/Wheeling Power customers a full extra year of grandfathering runway beyond what the company originally requested.
nem_aggregate_cap: 3% of aggregate WV peak demand (state default; 0.5% reserved for residential); AEP-WV-specific subscription level not published in sources reviewed
export_credit_value: ~12.4 cents/kWh fixed export credit for new (post-grandfathering-deadline) customers; 1:1 full retail for customers who applied by 2/28/2026
ic_study_trigger_kw: Level 2 required for systems not meeting Level 1 criteria (effectively >25 kW or non-UL-1741-SB-certified equipment)
external_disconnect: Required — labeled, lockable, visible load-break disconnect required outside near the utility meter per AEP TIIR
standby_charge: None identified — the 2025 PSC order restructured the export credit rate rather than adding a distinct standby/demand charge
storage_specific_notes: Not directly addressed in sources reviewed; because grandfathering is keyed to interconnection APPLICATION DATE rather than a system-composition test, adding a battery to an already-grandfathered (pre-2/28/2026) system likely does not by itself forfeit 1:1 status, but this is not explicitly confirmed by AEP-WV public materials and should be verified directly (flagged in gaps file).

rule_summary: Wheeling Power is a party to the same joint PSC base-rate/net-metering case as Appalachian Power Co (AEP-WV), decided August 2025. Same grandfathering mechanics apply: customers whose net metering interconnection application was submitted by February 28, 2026 retain full 1:1 retail crediting; later applicants receive the fixed ~12.4 cents/kWh export credit (67-75% of full retail rate). Wheeling Power's WV service territory is limited to the Wheeling/Ohio County area.
nem_aggregate_cap: 3% of aggregate WV peak demand (state default; 0.5% reserved for residential); Wheeling-Power-specific subscription level not published in sources reviewed
export_credit_value: ~12.4 cents/kWh fixed export credit for new (post-grandfathering-deadline) customers; 1:1 full retail for customers who applied by 2/28/2026
ic_study_trigger_kw: Level 2 required for systems not meeting Level 1 criteria
external_disconnect: Required — labeled, lockable, visible load-break disconnect required outside near the utility meter per AEP TIIR
standby_charge: None identified — same as AEP-WV; export credit rate restructured rather than a separate standby charge
storage_specific_notes: Same as AEP-WV: grandfathering keyed to interconnection application date; battery-addition-to-existing-system treatment not explicitly confirmed in public materials (flagged in gaps file).

rule_summary: Per the Feb. 16, 2024 PSC-approved settlement (effective March 27, 2024) resolving the companies' net-energy-metering base-rate case: customers who were net metering customers BEFORE the settlement's cutover are grandfathered onto full 1:1 retail bill offset for 25 years. New NEM customers interconnecting ON OR AFTER January 1, 2025 receive fixed credit rates instead of 1:1: 9.34 cents/kWh (residential, schools, churches, general service), 9.15 cents/kWh (large general service), 8.91 cents/kWh (large power/alternative generation). These new-customer rates are fixed for 2025-2026 and subject to renegotiation in the companies' 2026 ENEC (Expanded Net Energy Cost) case. Excess is credited only against the energy portion of the bill, not fixed/demand charges.
nem_aggregate_cap: 3% of aggregate WV peak demand (state default; Mon Power-specific subscription level not published in sources reviewed)
export_credit_value: New customers (on/after 1/1/2025): 9.34c/kWh (residential/schools/churches/general service), 9.15c/kWh (large general service), 8.91c/kWh (large power/alternative generation); legacy/grandfathered customers: 1:1 full retail for 25 years from settlement effective date
standby_charge: None identified in sources reviewed — settlement restructured the export credit rate itself rather than adding a standby charge
storage_specific_notes: Grandfathering (1:1 for 25 years) is tied to being an EXISTING net metering customer as of the March 27, 2024 settlement cutover, not to system composition; whether adding a battery to an existing grandfathered system requires a new interconnection application that could jeopardize the 25-year grandfathering is not explicitly addressed in sources reviewed (flagged in gaps file).

rule_summary: Identical settlement terms to Monongahela Power (same joint 2024 PSC case, same company parent FirstEnergy): customers who were net metering customers before the March 27, 2024 settlement cutover are grandfathered onto full 1:1 retail bill offset for 25 years. New NEM customers interconnecting on/after January 1, 2025 receive fixed credit rates: 9.34 cents/kWh (residential/schools/churches/general service), 9.15 cents/kWh (large general service), 8.91 cents/kWh (large power/alternative generation), fixed for 2025-2026 and subject to renegotiation in the 2026 ENEC case. Excess credited only against the energy portion of the bill.
nem_aggregate_cap: 3% of aggregate WV peak demand (state default; Potomac Edison-WV-specific subscription level not published in sources reviewed)
export_credit_value: New customers (on/after 1/1/2025): 9.34c/kWh (residential/schools/churches/general service), 9.15c/kWh (large general service), 8.91c/kWh (large power/alternative generation); legacy/grandfathered customers: 1:1 full retail for 25 years from settlement effective date
storage_specific_notes: Same as Monongahela Power: grandfathering tied to being an existing customer as of 3/27/2024, not to system composition; battery-addition impact on grandfathering not explicitly addressed in sources reviewed (flagged in gaps file).

rule_summary: NOVEC is an electric cooperative and operates net metering under Va. Code § 56-594.01 (separate from the IOU statute) via its NEM-10 rider, not under SCC IOU net metering rules directly. Program active since 2003. Individual system cap: 20 kW AC residential, up to 1 MW nonresidential. Program-wide aggregate cap: 2.0% of NOVEC's system peak load for residential and nonjurisdictional/nonprofit customers, 1.0% of system peak for other nonresidential customers (statewide co-op default under § 56-594.01). Exact credit rate, true-up mechanics, and current subscription level are not published in detail on NOVEC's public materials.
nem_aggregate_cap: 2% of NOVEC system peak (residential/nonjurisdictional); 1% of system peak (other nonresidential)
export_credit_value: Not published in detail on public page
standby_charge: Unknown — not addressed in public materials reviewed
standby_threshold_kw: Not applicable (no standby charge identified for NOVEC)
storage_specific_notes: Not addressed in NOVEC's public net metering materials reviewed; NOVEC does separately offer an EV-1 time-of-use rate applied to whole-home usage, described as not applicable to net metering (billed under a separate rider).

rule_summary: REC operates net metering under its Net Energy Metering Rider (2023) pursuant to Va. Code § 56-594.01 (co-op-specific statute). Individual system cap: 20 kW AC residential, 1,000 kW AC nonresidential; system may not be sized to produce more than 100% of the customer's trailing 12-month usage. 1:1 kWh credit with indefinite monthly rollover of banked credits. After 12 months on the program, customers may optionally elect a Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) that buys out banked excess kWh at REC's avoided wholesale cost (roughly 30-40% of retail rate), zeroing the bank. REC also offers a separate Community Solar Rider (SSR) sold in 50 kWh blocks, available to any residential member regardless of net metering status. REC's TOU rate (Schedule A-1-TOU) is explicitly NOT available to net metering customers.
nem_aggregate_cap: Program-wide aggregate limited by rate class; residential aggregate approximately 5.4% of REC's system peak load remaining as of August 2026 (self-reported, not independently verified)
aggregate_cap_status: ~5.4% of residential program headroom remaining as of Aug. 2026 (per REC public reporting)
export_credit_value: 1:1 retail credit during banking; optional PPA buyout of excess after 12 months at ~30-40% of retail (avoided wholesale cost)
external_disconnect: Required — external disconnect language present in REC interconnection materials, exact spec not detailed in sources reviewed
standby_charge: Unknown — not addressed in public materials reviewed for battery-specific treatment
standby_threshold_kw: Not applicable (no standby charge identified for REC)
storage_specific_notes: Not directly addressed in REC's public Net Metering Rider materials reviewed; battery addition to an existing net-metered system not explicitly discussed (flagged in gaps file). REC's Schedule A-1-TOU rate is explicitly incompatible with net metering, which matters for storage+TOU-arbitrage designs.

rule_summary: SVEC operates residential net metering under Va. Code § 56-594.01 with a cap of the LESSER of 20 kW AC (for systems installed on/after 7/1/2015) or the customer's expected annual consumption based on trailing 12-month billing history. Liability insurance required: $100,000 for systems <=10 kW, $300,000 for systems >10 kW. 1:1 volumetric credit netted against consumption; exact true-up/rollover mechanics not published in detail on SVEC's public page (governed by the VA SCC's co-op net metering order). SVEC notes that Dominion's net metering rules do NOT apply within SVEC's territory — SVEC sets its own terms under the co-op statute.
nem_aggregate_cap: Not published in detail on public page
export_credit_value: Not published in detail on public page
external_disconnect: Insurance required in lieu of disconnect specification: $100,000 (<=10 kW) / $300,000 (>10 kW)
standby_charge: Unknown — not addressed in public materials reviewed
standby_threshold_kw: Not applicable (no standby charge identified for SVEC)
storage_specific_notes: Not addressed in SVEC's public net metering materials reviewed (flagged in gaps file). SVEC separately offers a Renewable Energy Option Rider R and Community Solar program alongside net metering.

rule_summary: CVEC operates net metering under Schedule NEM-10 pursuant to Va. Code § 56-594.01. Individual system cap: 20 kW AC residential, 1 MW nonresidential. No application fee; $50 inspection fee. Insurance required: $100,000 for systems <=10 kW, $300,000 for systems >10-20 kW residential. 1:1 volumetric credit with monthly rollover of excess. Aggregate NEM-10 program cap (as of 4/15/2025): Residential 11,425 kW total allocation with 35% remaining headroom; Commercial 2,856 kW total with 75.4% remaining; Nonprofit/non-jurisdictional 5,712 kW total with 65% remaining. CVEC also offers a Solar Share community solar program under a separate SCC-approved Community Solar Order, which does NOT require combination with net metering.
nem_aggregate_cap: Residential 11,425 kW (35% remaining as of 4/15/2025); Commercial 2,856 kW (75.4% remaining); Nonprofit/non-jurisdictional 5,712 kW (65% remaining)
aggregate_cap_status: Residential 35% headroom remaining, Commercial 75.4% remaining, Nonprofit 65% remaining, all as of 4/15/2025
standby_charge: Unknown — not addressed in public materials reviewed
standby_threshold_kw: Not applicable (no standby charge identified for CVEC)
storage_specific_notes: Not addressed in CVEC's public net metering materials reviewed (flagged in gaps file). CVEC's Solar Share community solar program is explicitly NOT required to combine with net metering, giving members an alternative path.

rule_summary: BARC operates net metering under Schedule NEM-10 pursuant to Va. Code § 56-594.01, with a Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) option available for excess generation buyout (terms not published in detail). Aggregate program caps (as of May 2026): Residential 4% of BARC's system peak (2,754.6 kW total allocation, ~519 kW available); Nonresidential 1% of system peak (550.9 kW available); Nonprofit/non-jurisdictional 2% of system peak (48.3 kW available). Individual system size caps not published in detail beyond the co-op statewide default (20 kW AC residential).

utility_name: Danville Utilities (City of Danville - Division of Power & Light)
rule_summary: Danville is a municipal utility, exempt from SCC net metering jurisdiction; it sets its own Net Metering Policy. 1:1 volumetric credit netted monthly; excess generation carried forward to the next month (terms not published in full detail). Interconnection notice requirements: >=30 days advance notice required for systems <=25 kW; >=60 days advance notice required for systems >25 kW. Exact credit rate and annual/true-up treatment not published in detail on public materials.
nem_aggregate_cap: Not applicable (municipal utility; no SCC-mandated aggregate cap identified)
standby_charge: Unknown — not addressed in public materials reviewed
storage_specific_notes: Not addressed in Danville's public net metering materials reviewed (flagged in gaps file).

rule_summary: HEC is a municipal utility, exempt from SCC jurisdiction and Dominion's net metering rules per its own explicit disclosure ('Dominion net metering rules do not apply in Harrisonburg'). Under HEC's Net Metering Agreement, generation up to 100% of the customer's annual usage is credited at full retail 1:1 rate; generation between 100% and 200% of annual usage is credited at HEC's avoided cost of wholesale power (a materially lower rate). System may be sized up to 200% of annual usage, but only the first 100% receives full retail-value credit.
nem_cap_res_kw: Not published (system may be sized up to 200% of annual usage; only first 100% gets full retail credit)
nem_aggregate_cap: Not applicable (municipal utility; no SCC-mandated aggregate cap identified)
export_credit_value: 1:1 full retail for generation <=100% of annual usage; HEC's avoided cost of wholesale power for the portion of generation between 100-200% of annual usage
standby_charge: Unknown — not addressed in public materials reviewed
storage_specific_notes: Not addressed in HEC's public net metering materials reviewed (flagged in gaps file). The 100%/200% tiered-credit sizing rule is a significant deviation from the simple 1:1-up-to-annual-usage rule used elsewhere in VA, and matters for storage-augmented oversizing strategies.
